new_page.title: BC Home Buyer Rescission Period: 3 Days & the 0.25% Fee
new_page.h1: Can I back out of buying a home in BC after my offer is accepted?
new_page.description: BC buyers can cancel an accepted offer within three business days by written notice and paying 0.25% of the offer price. What it covers and what it doesn't.

breadcrumbs.name: Can I back out of buying a home in BC after my offer is accepted?

faq.q: Does the rescission period apply to presales?
faq.a: Presales from a developer are covered by their own cancellation right under BC's real estate development rules: seven days after receiving the disclosure statement.

faq.q: Can a seller back out during the three days?
faq.a: No. The right belongs to the buyer only.

parts.t: Yes, within three business days. Since January 3, 2023, a buyer of most homes in BC can cancel an accepted offer by giving the seller written notice before the rescission period ends and paying a fee of 0.25% of the offer price. On a $1,000,000 home the fee is $2,500.
Detached homes, semi-detached homes, townhouses, condos and other strata lots, units in duplexes and multi-unit buildings, manufactured homes on land, and co-op interests.

items.t: Homes on leased land and leasehold interests

parts.t: Weekends and statutory holidays do not count. Only the buyer can rescind, and the seller cannot ask the buyer to waive it.

blocks.text: Subjects are still the better protection

parts.t: The rescission period is short and costs money. Subject clauses for financing, inspection and strata documents give you time to check the home without a fee, so most buyers still write them in.
Read on November 18, 2026. Rules change, so confirm with the source or your lawyer, notary or accountant before you act.
